name: sign-in with retry
summary: The "sign in with retry" flow has 5 steps. It starts in *idle* and can end in *signed in* or *locked out*.

sentences.text: A visitor signs in with an email and a password.

states.text: *idle*: The flow starts here. The form is shown and editable.

events.text: "submit" (`SUBMIT`) is something that can happen, carrying `{ email: string; password: string }`.

transitions.text: In *idle*: When "submit" happens, the flow moves to *checking*.

functions.text: `verifyCredentials` takes `{ email: string; password: string }` and gives back `Promise<{ ok: true; session: Session } | { ok: false; reason: string }>`. It expects: email and password are both non-empty strings. It promises: Resolves { ok: true, session } when the pair matches an account; otherwise { ok: false, reason } with a reason that does not say which of the two was wrong.

sentences.text: While the credentials are being checked, the form is locked.

states.text: *checking*: A step of the flow. The form is locked while the credentials are verified.

transitions.text: In *idle*: When "submit" happens, the flow moves to *checking*.

sentences.text: If the credentials are valid, the visitor is signed in and taken to their dashboard.

states.text: *signed in*: An end state, the flow stops here. The visitor has a session and is on the dashboard.

events.text: "valid" (`VALID`) is something that can happen, carrying `{ session: Session }`.

transitions.text: In *checking*: When "valid" happens, the flow moves to *signed in*.

functions.text: `verifyCredentials` takes `{ email: string; password: string }` and gives back `Promise<{ ok: true; session: Session } | { ok: false; reason: string }>`. It expects: email and password are both non-empty strings. It promises: Resolves { ok: true, session } when the pair matches an account; otherwise { ok: false, reason } with a reason that does not say which of the two was wrong.
`openDashboard` takes `Session` and gives back `void`. It expects: The session was just issued by verifyCredentials. It promises: The browser is on the dashboard route with the session attached.

sentences.text: If the credentials are invalid, the visitor sees the reason and can try again.

states.text: *failed*: A step of the flow. The reason is shown; the form is editable again.

events.text: "invalid" (`INVALID`) is something that can happen, carrying `{ reason: string }`.
"retry" (`RETRY`) is something that can happen, carrying nothing.

transitions.text: In *checking*: Otherwise, the flow moves to *failed*.
In *failed*: When "retry" happens, the flow moves to *idle*.

functions.text: `verifyCredentials` takes `{ email: string; password: string }` and gives back `Promise<{ ok: true; session: Session } | { ok: false; reason: string }>`. It expects: email and password are both non-empty strings. It promises: Resolves { ok: true, session } when the pair matches an account; otherwise { ok: false, reason } with a reason that does not say which of the two was wrong.

sentences.text: After three failed attempts in a row, the visitor is locked out and must reset their password.

states.text: *locked out*: An end state, the flow stops here. No more attempts; only a password reset gets the visitor out.

transitions.text: In *checking*: When "invalid" happens, the flow moves to *locked out* — only if the "attempts exhausted" condition holds.

functions.text: `recordFailedAttempt` takes `{ attempts: number }` and gives back `{ attempts: number; exhausted: boolean }`. It expects: attempts is a non-negative integer (0 before the first failure). It promises: attempts is one higher than the input; exhausted is true exactly when the new count is 3 or more.

sentences.text: The sign-in page must load in under two seconds.
sentences.reason: A performance budget, not machine behaviour: checked by a Lighthouse threshold in CI, not by this workflow.

types.text: `Session` is `{ userId: string; token: string }`: What a successful sign-in hands back.
